title: fix: mint request_id server-side instead of trusting the client header
author: davealan74
pr_body_excerpt:
## Bug

`requestId()` (hono's built-in middleware) was mounted bare in both
`gen.pollinations.ai/src/index.ts` and `enter.pollinations.ai/src/index.ts`.
At the pinned hono version it accepts an inbound `X-Request-Id` header
verbatim (if it passes a length/charset check) and echoes it back, so any
caller can pin an arbitrary id or replay one they observed elsewhere.

## Root cause

Trusting a client-supplied id for something used internally as a stable,
unique per-request key breaks two things downstream:
- `image/models/novaReelModel.ts` interpolates the request id into a fixed
  S3 prefix and reads `{prefix}/output.mp4` back — two callers sharing an id
  share the S3 key.
- `request_id` is the only join key between a fallback-attempt row and its
  settlement row, so a replayed id corrupts that grouping.

## Fix

- Add `shared/middleware/request-id.ts`: always mints via
  `crypto.randomUUID()`, `c.set("requestId", id)`, and still sets the
  `X-Request-Id` response header — same `RequestIdVariables` shape as hono's
  version, so no `env.ts` type changes were needed.
- Swap the `hono/request-id` import for the shared middleware in both
  `gen.pollinations.ai/src/index.ts` and `enter.pollinations.ai/src/index.ts`.
- Add `gen.pollinations.ai/test/request-id.test.ts`: mounts the middleware on
  a bare Hono app, sends a spoofed `X-Request-Id`, and asserts the response
  header differs from the sent value, matches `c.get("requestId")`, and is a
  valid UUID.

Fixes #12889

gist.headline: IDs grow in the hive
gist.blurb: Request IDs are now grown fresh at the server door, where they belong. Every trip through the hive gets its own tidy little UUID.
gist.summary: Added shared server-side request ID middleware for both gen.pollinations.ai and enter.pollinations.ai, minting a fresh crypto.randomUUID() for every request while preserving the X-Request-Id response header.
gist.impact: Video output lookups and fallback settlement records now receive reliably unique per-request keys, keeping concurrent requests cleanly separated.
gist.visual_concept: Polli is a careful postal clerk in a cozy garden-server shed, stamping freshly grown UUID labels onto separate glowing request parcels before they travel down distinct vine-lined routes to a video reel shelf and a settlement ledger. The scene represents server-minted identifiers keeping each request, output, and record in its own place.
